*After reading this note you will be able to define obesity and metabolic syndrome, list the local aetiologies, describe the key pathophysiological steps and recognise the essential clinical findings.

qs.q: Metabolic syndrome diagnosis requires at least 3 of 5 criteria. These are
o: Fever, leukocytosis, raised C‑reactive protein, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and lymphocytosis.
Central obesity, hypertension, high triglycerides, low HDL cholesterol, and elevated fasting glucose.
Peripheral edema, proteinuria, increased LDL cholesterol, hyperkalemia, and high plasma renin activity.
Hypoglycaemia, bradycardia, low LDL cholesterol, underweight body habitus, and low blood pressure.
qs.e: Greatly increases CV risk and T2DM risk. Associated with NAFLD, PCOS, sleep apnoea.
